profile.headline: Software Engineer | Autonomous Systems & Standards Development | Java, C++, DevOps
profile.summary:
I build software for autonomous systems, and I have a habit of fixing the slow, fragile, and manual processes that hold teams back.

I'm a software engineer who works across the full stack of complex systems: developing technical standards, implementing them in software, and even taking autonomous vehicles out into the field for testing. I've contributed to UMAA (Unmanned Maritime Autonomy Architecture), a publicly released standard used across industry and government for autonomy interoperability. I gravitate toward the problems most people avoid: modernizing build systems, untangling complicated toolchains, and building the reusable libraries, automated checks, and pipelines that make an entire team faster.

A few things that define how I work:
• I care deeply about efficiency and craftsmanship: writing code that is fast, resource-conscious, and maintainable, and building tooling that makes development more enjoyable for everyone around me.
• I like working across boundaries: standards, application code, DevOps, and even hardware.
• Above all, I'm driven by learning. I set aside time to pick up something new almost every day, whether it's a new technology at work or Vietnamese in my free time.

I hold a B.S. in Computer Science from Illinois State University, and my early career in mentoring students and automating business processes still shapes how I work today. Whether it's eliminating tedious work or helping the people around me grow, that's the kind of impact I care about most.

positions.title: R&D Software Engineer
positions.locationName: State College, Pennsylvania, United States · Hybrid
positions.description:
• Unmanned Maritime Autonomy Architecture (UMAA) Specification Working Group (SWG): Reduced the specification build pipeline from 3 hours to 15 minutes by transitioning to an internal Groovy-based DSL for model definition; developed a decompiler to regenerate source code into a parseable format.
• Presented technical designs and demonstrations to the cross-organization UMAA standards board, translating complex implementation details for both technical and non-technical audiences.
• UMAA Reference Implementation Working Group (RWG): Designed and implemented a reusable Java library for UMAA service and component implementations using an interface-based architecture with 94% unit test coverage.
• Developed a vehicle dynamics simulator with simplified pitch/depth and yaw control for an in-house vehicle platform, enabling software-in-the-loop testing without requiring physical hardware.
• Led on-water testing and hardware maintenance for an IVER AUV; diagnosed and resolved recurring electronics and communications issues; performed root-cause analyses for safety-trigger incidents.
• Owned and facilitated Agile ceremonies, including standups, sprint planning, backlog refinement, and retrospectives; mentored engineers while encouraging a growth-oriented approach to challenging technical problems.
• UMAA Software Development Kit (SDK): Lead developer for a one-click graphical simulation of a vehicle completing a series of waypoints; established modern C++ coding standards through code reviews and style guides; deployed the application with Docker Compose and automated CI/CD in GitLab.
• Built an LLM tool server for Cameo Systems Modeler: Developed a Gradle plugin for building Cameo plugins; implemented an OpenAPI wrapper around Cameo's Java API; deployed a containerized vLLM/Open-WebUI stack.

company.name: The Applied Research Laboratory at Penn State University

positions.title: Information Technology Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
• Graded parallel programming assignments implemented with MPI, OpenMP, Pthreads, and CUDA, executed on external HPC clusters (SDSC Expanse).
• Wrote shell scripts to automate the compilation and testing of student programs, improving grading consistency and turnaround time.
• Evaluated C, C++, and Java programming assignments and provided constructive, actionable feedback to support student improvement.
• Identified concepts students found challenging and surfaced them to strengthen future instruction.

positions.title: Information Technology Tutor
positions.description:
• Supported Health Information Management (HIM) students in learning the fundamentals of programming in Java.
• Diagnosed issues in student code and explained potential solutions, adapting explanations to each student's skill level.
• Clarified programming concepts based on individual student needs to reinforce understanding.

positions.title: NSF NexSTEM Peer Mentor
positions.description:
• Met weekly with mentees to foster a sense of belonging and support their transition into STEM studies.
• Helped mentees develop key skills, including time management and decision-making.
• Connected mentees with on-campus resources and opportunities to support their academic success.

positions.title: Robotic Process Automation (RPA) Developer
positions.description:
• Developed new automation bots by gathering and analyzing requirements from internal departments.
• Converted and redesigned bot scripts from Nintex to UiPath during a platform migration.
• Created reusable templates and libraries to accelerate bot development and establish reliable coding conventions.
• Executed and monitored existing bots, reporting and troubleshooting errors as they arose.

• Lead a workshop by demonstrating and helping the children complete a technical activity.

projects.title: Neuron Synchronization Simulation (C & Python)
projects.description:
• Implemented Euler’s and Runge-Kutta's (RK4) numerical methods for approximating ordinary differential equations.
• Implemented the Hindmarsh-Rose (HR) model with an added coupling factor to simulate the behavior of coupled neurons.
• Used Python’s NetworkX library to generate graphs (adjacency matrices) representing the coupling strengths between neurons in the simulation.
• Used Gnuplot to visualize the results of the simulation.
